pr:144.body:
The README exposes a downloadable binary, but it pins the command to one release and
does not identify that path as the quickest first run. Readers have to infer which
deployment mode fits their host, and binary or local-mode startup failures have no
single recovery path. This change makes the published binary path, the advanced Docker
path, and local development path explicit in both languages without adding promises
about the release process.

## Summary

- Point both READMEs to the generic Releases page, show the x86_64 and arm64 asset
  naming pattern, and identify the prepackaged binary as the shortest first-run path.
- Add an operating-system column to both deployment-mode comparisons. Docker is now
  explicitly framed as an advanced container-operations option, while local mode is
  framed for development and debugging.
- Lead the binary deployment sections with downloading and starting a published asset,
  before the existing source-build procedure.
- Add matching first-run troubleshooting for binary and local mode: rejected local
  service access tokens, `degraded` health, missing Bubblewrap, and log locations.
  Link it from both READMEs and quick starts.
- Apply #46's release-link and deployment-ordering asks. Leave its published-asset
  checksum verification, update and uninstall guidance, and configuration-entry naming
  to follow-up work that needs release-process confirmation.

This implements the installation-decision and first-run-recovery scope of #116, and the
release-link and deployment-ordering parts of #46. Refs #116. Relates to #46.

## Validation

- `pnpm docs:check` passes: markdownlint reports 0 issues, and the relative-link check
  passes across 89 Markdown files.
- `git diff --check` is clean.
- An independent review verified all six acceptance criteria and walked the documentation
  as a new user, an installed task user, and an advanced user choosing a deployment mode.
- No product code changed, so no UT, ST, or E2E test layers were run.

## E2E user journeys

**Not applicable.** This change only updates Markdown. The lint and relative-link checks
cover Markdown formatting and relative target files. The independent review checked the
new reader paths and their fragments in the three user journeys described above.

## Release

Release category: release:docs

User impact: new users can choose a current binary asset without copying a stale release
URL, recognize Docker as an advanced path, and recover from the most common binary or
local-mode first-run failures.

Compatibility and migration: none.

pr:145.body:
## Summary

Both distribution paths (the single-file binary and the Docker image) now carry JiuwenSwarm and the sciencediscovery adapter themselves, instead of requiring a separate source-mode install — and both now run on JiuwenSwarm by default. JiuwenSwarm is installed straight from its PyPI release (`workswarm==0.2.6`), not cloned: the pinned tag's PyPI publish resolves its git-pinned transitive dependency (`openjiuwen`) as a plain PyPI version, so no cloning or wheel-building is needed on either path.

- **Release binary**: `build-payload.sh` installs the adapter and JiuwenSwarm into flat, `PYTHONPATH`-addressable site-packages directories (not a venv, whose shebangs/`pyvenv.cfg` would hardcode the build machine's path and break once extracted elsewhere). The launcher (`services/launcher`) starts both alongside the API when running in JiuwenSwarm mode, wiring the same ports/env vars `start-stack.sh` uses in source mode. **Defaults to JiuwenSwarm** — `--no-jiuwenswarm` (or `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=native`) switches back to the native loop.
- **Docker image**: the builder stage bakes the adapter's venv the same way paper/gateway already are (its own `uv.lock`, locked sync), plus a separate JiuwenSwarm venv straight from PyPI. `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh` gained `JIUWENSWARM_SRC` (independent of `JIUWENSWARM_ROOT`): the image bakes the read-only venv under `/opt`, while the instance's own state stays under the bind-mounted data directory, so it survives a container recreation. `start-stack.sh --mode docker` **also defaults to JiuwenSwarm** now (`--no-jiuwenswarm` to opt out) and runs the now-idempotent `jiuwenswarm.sh setup` automatically on first start, since a container has no separate shell to run a one-time setup step in beforehand.
- **Local/source mode is unaffected** — still native by default, `--jiuwenswarm` opts in, since it requires a separate `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` step (git clone).

## Bug fixes along the way

- `agent_runs.py`: a cancel racing a pending approval could crash the whole adapter process (unhandled send-on-closed-websocket); now a handled no-op.
- Pinned `native-agent/versioning.test.ts` and raised `run-cancel.test.ts`'s timing budget (200×25ms → 400×25ms) after auditing against a real JiuwenSwarm instance.
- `uv pip install --python-version 3.12` doesn't satisfy a locally built wheel's `Requires-Python>=3.12` (that gate checks the actual interpreter, not the flag) — switched to `--python 3.12`, which still resolves via `--python-platform` for cross-arch builds.
- The build-machine-path leak check (`assert_no_build_paths`) false-positived across JiuwenSwarm's own ~1GB third-party tree (an XML `</root>` tag, SSH tooling's `/root/.ssh`, JiuwenSwarm's own `.worktrees`-based sandboxing feature) — scoped the generic `$HOME`/`.worktrees` needles out of the two third-party install directories, while the specific `$repository_root`/`$shared_dir`/`$output` needles (which catch a real leak, e.g. the adapter wheel's `direct_url.json`) stay fully scanned everywhere.
- **Real data-loss bug**, caught by actually recreating a container against the same data dir rather than trusting one successful start: JiuwenSwarm's instance workspace lives under `$HOME/.jiuwenswarm-instances/`, with no option to move it. The previous HOME fallback only redirected to the data dir when the container's own HOME was unwritable — the `node` user's default HOME is writable, so every container recreation would have silently started a brand-new instance. Fixed to force HOME onto the data dir whenever the adapter is running.

## Test plan

- [x] Real `docker build` and `docker build`-equivalent binary build, both succeeding end to end (not just typechecked)
- [x] Ran the built binary with `--jiuwenswarm`: `/agent/info` reports `executor: "jiuwenswarm"`, `reachable: true`
- [x] Ran the Docker image with **no flags**: same result — confirms the new default
- [x] Ran the Docker image with `--no-jiuwenswarm`: confirms native loop, no adapter, no real `/agent/info`
- [x] Destroyed and recreated a Docker container against the same data directory: confirmed the JiuwenSwarm instance and auth token both persisted instead of resetting
- [x] `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/launcher test`: 115/115 passing

pr:146.body:
## Summary

Repair the Swarm-backed research path exposed by DeepResearchBench debugging: children must see their specialist MCP tools, keep their own model route, and return without a single tool failure poisoning the shared transport or crashing the API.

This PR targets `feat/jiuwenswarm` from a personal fork. It retains **ScienceDiscovery `task` orchestration + Swarm execution for both main and child agents**. Native Swarm delegation reuse remains an explicit follow-up in #141; this PR does not claim to implement or validate native `subagent_spawn` inheritance. Related: #107, #136.

## Changes and scope

- Carry four reviewable, version-pinned `workswarm0.2.6` compatibility patches under `jiuwen_swarm/patches`, applied idempotently during setup/start: refresh the dynamic `sci` MCP catalog without disconnecting active clients; honor configured MCP timeouts without competing default wrappers; resolve newly published run-model aliases; preserve stream request IDs across the TUI transport; give the platform MCP transport a stable lifecycle owner and remove its competing HTTP read deadline.
- Correlate approval-resume streams: ignore retired streams' terminal events before mapping run status, while preserving late usage accounting. Do not finish a run while approval is pending. Map execution/runtime errors to terminal failures instead of silently waiting for the idle timeout.
- Preserve CAS references atomically when sanitizing large tool details. Improve invalid-reference diagnostics and catch bridge dispatch/persistence failures as non-retryable, unknown-outcome tool errors rather than allowing an unhandled rejection to terminate the API.
- Propagate bridge disconnect cancellation to the affected tool/child; enforce task wall-clock deadlines including model/tool waits; honor smaller budgets when the default subagent preset is implicit.
- Keep NDJSON transports alive without fabricating progress; add opt-in tool-contract diagnostics; clarify that sandbox writes use workspace-relative paths.
- Add tests and reproduction documentation. Scientific business logic is not moved into Swarm. Existing web-provider settings remain unchanged.

## End-to-end coverage

| Case | What it exercises | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test/swarm-research-mocked.spec.ts` | Browser → API → actual Swarm main loop → platform task → actual Swarm child loop/MCP bridge → failed shell call → recovery → child artifact → parent report → UI | **Passed after the transport fix**, 1 case, 55.8 s overall |
| `test/deepresearchbench-swarm.spec.ts` | Real model, DRB-59, two literature specialists, successful literature MCP use, completed children, parent continuation, registered report and visible final response | **Still failed** (18.0 min): long task results now return and parent resumes, but one child stalled and the run did not deliver a final report; final status request returned API 502 |

The Mock case uses scripted local LLM responses and synthetic source notes; it tests framework recovery, not model intelligence or scientific quality. Dynamic MCP catalog refresh and exact model routing have separate pinned-Swarm regression checks.

Before the browser run, an API-driven real GLM-5.2 DRB-59 run completed in **513.644 s**: both children completed (11 turns each), actual child model requests included the 12 enabled literature tools, PubMed/Europe PMC calls succeeded, and the parent registered a **17,878-byte** report. An arXiv HTTP 406 remained an external tool failure; the model used alternative sources. This is supporting integration evidence, **not a DeepResearchBench score** and not a substitute for the pending real browser test.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Adapter Python tests: gateway, events, agent runs, LLM proxy, MCP server | 137 passed; the 5 new approval-race/error regressions were confirmed failing before the fix |
| Pinned Swarm dynamic-catalog/model-route/stream-ID regressions | 4 passed |
| Platform MCP loopback transport regressions | 8 passed (4.4 s): no hidden read deadline, concurrent correlation, isolated tool timeout/cancellation, disconnect/failure propagation, explicit reconnect, forced HTTP read-timeout regression |
| Swarm Node adapter test file | 65 passed |
| Tool registry + subagent configuration | 20 passed |
| Hard child wall-clock timeout integration | Passed |
| Workspace task-schema regression | Passed |
| Browser Mock E2E | 1 passed |
| E2E metadata validation | Passed; 11 pre-existing legacy warnings |
| Markdown lint, shell syntax, patch reverse-apply checks, diff whitespace | Passed |
| Final API build and repeated Python suite | Interrupted by host incident; no completed result claimed |

The test host has ~3.4 GiB RAM. At approximately 20:24 CST on September 22, a build overlapped with the live browser research run. System logs later recorded service watchdog timeouts, and the host rebooted at 21:02. No OOM-killer record was found; resource contention is suspected, not established. TypeScript 7 launches a native compiler, so the Node heap option did not constrain the compiler. Heavy checks were not automatically restarted. Documentation now calls for serial build/test phases on constrained hosts.

## How to reproduce / remaining work

See `jiuwen_swarm/README.md` for commands, model credential options, tool tracing and the explicit Swarm/task deployment boundary. Mock E2E is enabled in the CI Swarm stack; real API E2E is opt-in and billable. No keys, local auth tokens, raw model prompts, or runtime databases are committed.

### Latest instrumented rerun (September 22)

An earlier instrumented failure exposed an approval race: a retired request's completion ended a resumed child and removed its live model route. Commit `e0d23cd5` fixes this race with transport request correlation; deterministic regressions fail before the fix and pass after it.

The subsequent real browser rerun still **failed**. Both children completed (12 and 14 turns), used PubMed/Europe PMC, and registered artifacts. Browser SSE includes both platform `task` completion events, but the Swarm log has no corresponding real-run `Tool 'task' call completed` entry and the parent idled out after 240 seconds. This narrows the remaining investigation to result delivery between the platform bridge and Swarm's waiting MCP invocation; the precise cause is not established. The closed-model-client error was not observed in this rerun. No timeout or assertion was relaxed.

The missing result-delivery cause was subsequently reproduced: OpenJiuwen passed only `timeout` to the MCP SDK's deprecated HTTP transport factory, leaving its separate HTTP read timeout at 300 seconds. The platform endpoint returns JSON only when the task finishes. A background transport failure could strand callers because the SDK contexts were opened by a prewarm task rather than a lifetime owner.

Commits `4f8c7a0a` / `274476f1` scope the fix to the platform `sci` client. A dedicated owner opens/closes SDK contexts in the same task; pending calls race against owner termination and fail promptly. HTTP reads have no independent deadline; configured per-tool deadlines remain enforced, and cancelling one request does not kill its siblings. Other external MCP clients are unchanged. No automatic action replay was added.

The latest real rerun confirms both task results reached Swarm after approximately **392 s and 469 s**, exceeding the former 300 s deadline, and the parent continued with `read_file`. One child completed in 12 turns; the other returned an explicit 240000 ms idle failure after 11 turns. The parent later had file-read errors and a model `idle_chunk` timeout (60 s); the test ultimately failed on a status API 502/ReadError at 18.0 minutes. The report was not completed. These remaining failures are not waived or claimed fixed by the transport patch.

The runs used an isolated cgroup (2,300 MiB memory maximum, 256 MiB swap maximum, 150% CPU), continuous resource/kernel logging, and no concurrent builds. No cgroup OOM or OOM kill was recorded. Raw browser traces and process diagnostics are retained privately because they may contain credentials. Test services were stopped after archiving results.

**Not ready to claim full real-E2E recovery.** Before merge, investigate the remaining child/parent execution and API failures and obtain passing CI. The preceding CI head also failed two journey cases and the host-shell isolation check; these are not waived. The long-running gateway `agent_run_slow` / `agent_run_recover` scenarios were not rerun in this final validation batch. Full UT/ST/E2E was not run locally. Official DRB grading, all five benchmark cases, public-source availability fixes, and the native-delegation decision are outside this PR.

### Evaluation records and dashboard boundary (September 23)

The version-wide performance dashboard is owned by a separate developer/workstream and is **not part of this PR**. This work supplies per-attempt evaluation/performance records for that dashboard to ingest later; it does not implement dashboard UI, storage ingestion, aggregation or scheduling.

The follow-up test changes are currently local and have **not yet been pushed to this PR head**:
- Remove the real DRB-59 test's fixed two-child / 3–5-source / per-child test-prompt limits. Keep configurable harness execution deadlines and existing runtime budgets.
- Separate deterministic delivery checks (terminal completion, research activity, readable declared report and persistence across reload) from RACE/FACT quality gates. Recovered child failures remain reliability metrics rather than failing only because a replacement child increased the count.
- Run the pinned upstream RACE/FACT pipeline with configurable Judge credentials and explicit partial/error states. Missing credentials or failed retrievals must not become passing quality results.

Record locations in each retained Playwright attempt:
- `benchmark-metrics.json`: schema version, case/run/generator identity, timestamps, exact prompt, execution budgets, integration status, duration, raw generation usage, child statuses and evaluation result.
- `deepresearchbench-59.json`: original benchmark question and exact persisted report.
- `evaluation/scorecard.json`: quality status, mode, thresholds, RACE/FACT scores, Judge models/backend, evaluator revision, report/reference hashes, evaluation duration and per-call Judge usage.
- `evaluation/judge-{input,output}-*.json` and FACT intermediate files: reproducibility/debug evidence; retain privately because research content may be sensitive.

Consumers must distinguish integration success from quality success, preserve failed/incomplete attempts, and treat missing scores as absent/null rather than zero. `race`-only / disabled evaluation is not a full-quality pass. RACE values are stored in 0–1 (50/100 means parity with the reference); FACT accuracy must be interpreted together with verification coverage. Generator and Judge token usage are separate streams. Do not combine unlike Judge models, evaluator revisions, prompts or thresholds as comparable scores.

The local record contract is documented in `test/benchmarks/deepresearchbench/README.md`. The dashboard owner can consume these records once this follow-up is pushed; no dashboard implementation is included.

Additional evidence, not a full E2E pass: the latest local real Swarm run completed and declared its report in 872.356 seconds, but the strict earlier browser case failed because an initial child had a model-route startup failure and was replaced (three child records instead of two). A separate single-case RACE evaluation of that actual report scored **47.49/100** using **GLM-5.2 as a substituted Judge**, not the official Judge. FACT was not run due to missing Jina credentials. This is not an official leaderboard result, does not validate the new full-quality E2E gate, and does not waive the remaining runtime/model-route defects.

pr:147.body:
## Summary

The GitHub `UT` job on `feat/jiuwenswarm` was hanging for the full 60-minute job timeout on every run. Root-caused and fixed the underlying bug, then ran the full `server.test.ts` + `run-cancel.test.ts` against a real JiuwenSwarm (`scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh`) to verify — which surfaced and fixed six more real, independent bugs, plus one systemic upstream limitation that isn't fixable here.

**Root cause, fixed:** every JiuwenSwarm-gated tool call recorded *two* `PermissionAuthorization` rows for one decision — `requestApproval` (runs/index.ts) records JiuwenSwarm's own ask before the call proceeds, then the tool's own `requirePrivilege` (workspace-bindings.ts) checked again once the call reached the bridge, with no idempotency between them. One of the three mid-run approval-mode-switch tests loops an unbounded `reader.read()` on a stream whose event accounting this double-booking threw off, and the host UT tier sets no `--test-timeout`, so nothing but the job's own 60-minute ceiling ever stopped it. `authorizeByJiuwenSwarm` now looks up an existing authorization by `toolCallId` before creating one.

**A second bug, fixed:** `startSubagentModel`'s scripted stub calls a tool literally named `task`, which JiuwenSwarm's own subagent-routing substitution deletes by default before a run starts. `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh` now sets `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_SUBAGENTS=task`, matching the same fix `.ci/run-e2e.sh` already needed.

**Six more bugs found and fixed while verifying against the full suite:**
- A JiuwenSwarm web-settings background sync retry loop had no lifecycle tie to server shutdown, so every short-lived test API server left it running against the one shared adapter for up to 15s — hundreds of them contending under `ci:ut:host`. Now aborts on server close.
- An authorization-count assertion raced session-title refinement sharing the run's model (loosened); which exposed `execution-runs` lagging `run.completed` by a beat under JiuwenSwarm (now polled); which exposed a stale assertion checking an environment-revision catalog the test harness's runner never populates regardless of executor (removed; that coverage belongs in `environment.test.ts`).
- A skill-deletion test was missing the `onJiuwenSwarm` branch its own neighboring assertion already had.
- A literature-flow test assumed `modelServer.requests[0]` was the run's own first call; a fresh instance's one-off skill-directory-tree call can land first.
- A cancel-replay test asserted `tool.started`, which under JiuwenSwarm only fires after approval (by design) — reads the call's arguments from `permission.required` instead under this executor.

**An upstream limitation, not fixed, quarantined:** once `task` correctly routes to our bridge, its nested round trip (a second `POST /agent/runs`) can leave JiuwenSwarm 0.2.6's gateway silent on the parent run's next turn until our idle-timeout watchdog fails it minutes later. Verified across 17 tests that delegate through `task`: **not deterministic per test** — one test passed three times in isolation, then failed the identical way in a longer run, pointing at load/state on the one shared JiuwenSwarm+adapter instance rather than a fixed set of bad tests. All 17 are now skipped under `onJiuwenSwarm` (not deleted — the coverage returns automatically once JiuwenSwarm fixes the stall), rather than building a per-test allowlist that would stay exposed to the same non-determinism.

`docs/{en,zh}/reference/jiuwenswarm-migration-status.md` record all of the above in detail.

## Test plan

- [x] Rebuilt `services/api` after every change (`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api build`)
- [x] Ran the full `server.test.js` + `run-cancel.test.js` against a real local JiuwenSwarm repeatedly during the investigation; final run: 77 pass, 17 skipped (documented gateway-stall quarantine), 2 fail (both pre-existing and unrelated — a known, already-documented occasional MCP-tool-visibility race, and a local machine missing an unrelated Python venv for the paper service)
- [x] Ran the same two files under the legacy/native loop: 95/96 pass (the one failure is the same pre-existing local venv issue), 0 skipped (confirms the skip only triggers under `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=jiuwenswarm`)
- [x] Ran `store.test.js` + `runs/index.test.js` + `workspace-bindings.test.js` + `jiuwenswarm-agent.test.js` + `http/*.test.js` + `environment*.test.js` (201 tests): 198 pass, 3 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (macOS lacks the bubblewrap sandbox a `workspace-bindings` test expects)
- [ ] Full `ci:ut:host` on Linux (CI will run this)

pr:148.body:
The UT, ST, and mocked E2E merge gates used to each keep their own handwritten command list, and a case could be skipped when the environment was missing. Tests now declare static tags in source. The three layers and a local `pnpm test:shared` select from that one plan, and a selected case must run. Corresponds to #126.

## Selection

The tags are orthogonal: `category`, `os`, `arch`, `npu`, `model`, `judge`, `status`, and `sandbox`. A plan is decided only by source, those tags, and a fixed profile. The current OS, credentials, NPU, or whether a service is up do not collect cases and do not rewrite the plan.

The `pr` profile is written as dimensions, and the selector is derived from them: linux/amd64, `npu:none`, `model` of none or mock, `judge:none`, `status:reviewed`. `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` are category slices of that plan. Their union is `pnpm test:shared`. GitHub Actions passes the profile as an argument (default `pr`), not as an environment variable, so the same command cannot select a different set on a different machine.

`daily` and `release` currently use the same rules as `pr`. Rows for a live model and for `judge:llm` stay in the profile shape until there are cases to put in them. Once those rows exist, missing credentials fail preflight instead of dropping the cases.

Preflight runs only after the plan is frozen. An unavailable sandbox, running as root, or a selected case whose environment is missing fails the whole run. Success means planned = executed = passed, with failed = 0 and skipped = 0. A missing results file is no longer treated as a pass.

`model` says whether the system under test uses a model. `judge` says whether the test asserts with an LLM. They are independent. There is no hybrid mode.

Cases that stay out of this plan, each with a tag and a reason in `test/support/tagged/MIGRATION.md`, include live-model, NPU, and legacy cases, cases that need a real Neo4j or SSH machine, and assertions that hold only on macOS.

## Fit with current main

The branch is rebased onto current main, and main's coverage jobs are kept. The five unit tests for the coverage scripts imported `node:test` directly, so the tagged collector never registered them and the UT slice would have left them out. They now declare the same static tags as the other script tests.

`pnpm test` is still build, binary:test, and each package's own tests. `ci:ut:host` and `ci:ut:guest` are gone. A case that needs bubblewrap says so with `sandbox:bubblewrap`, and preflight decides whether the whole plan can run. The CodeArts pipeline is no longer a gate.

## Validation

Commit `369729fad78123327a7329273215831d60b30f3f`, profile `pr`.

| Layer | planned | executed | passed | failed | skipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm ci:ut` | 3161 | 3161 | 3161 | 0 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:st` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:e2e` | 43 | 43 | 43 | 0 | 0 |

The three layers together are 3205 cases, the same set as `pnpm test:shared`. ST is the single mocked agent-loop case in `test/api/agent_loop_smoke.ts`.

## E2E user journeys

PASS. Commit under test: `369729fad78123327a7329273215831d60b30f3f`. Browser journeys on the mocked isolated stack. They do not use the local trial port.

`pnpm ci:e2e` runs 43 mocked Playwright journeys. Every planned journey has to pass. The result is 43 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

One attempt on this same commit failed first. In `journey-compact-process.spec.ts`, "Skill 入口按自己的任务与草稿状态去框" failed in 223ms because the data directory already contained the writable Skill library `project-skills`, so the "no writable library yet" state could not be reproduced. That directory was left by an earlier run of the same layer. It was not an assertion failure in this commit. After clearing that layer's data and keeping the already downloaded `data/envs`, as the test asks, the rerun passed all 43.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: nothing changes in the product UI or in the default way of using it. What changes is for developers and CI: the merge gate selects UT, ST, and mocked E2E from one static tag plan, and a skip is no longer a pass.

Compatibility and migration: the scope of `pnpm test` is unchanged. `ci:ut:host` and `ci:ut:guest` are removed; both are now `pnpm ci:ut`. Live-model, NPU, and legacy runs stay explicit entry points and are not in the default gate.

  回传评分和 insight，并在页面查看树结构与节点结果。树状态使用本地文件持久化，无需 Neo4j。

pr:51.body:
The README is the first and often only page a visitor reads, and it was not doing the three jobs it should. It opened with a one-sentence pitch and then a security disclaimer, so the second thing a reader met was the caveats. The four feature bullets were dense prose that linked nowhere — not to a doc, not to a tutorial, not to a screenshot. "Installation" never said where to obtain a binary, which is exactly what openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery#1 asked. The Chinese `项目定位` section repeated the intro verbatim while the English one described the architecture, so the two languages answered different questions. And neither README mentioned the CLI at all, while the English deployment guide omitted the `run` command the Chinese guide documents.

This reworks both READMEs around what a first-time reader needs, and closes the English/Chinese gap in the deployment guide.

## Both READMEs, restructured

Centered header with badges and a navigation row, one screenshot of the workspace, then: what it is, install, first task, what you can do, command line, requirements, how it works, documentation, license. The two files now have identical structure and make identical claims.

The capability table replaces the prose bullets. Every row links to the page that documents it, so each claim is something a reader can go and check rather than something they have to take on faith.

**The security warning is kept verbatim** — same text, not softened. It moves below the getting-started path so it reads as scope rather than as the product's opening statement.

## Getting started actually ends somewhere

`Install` now finishes the job: after `serve`, it says to open **http://127.0.0.1:4310** and sign in with the printed token, and states plainly that the terminal window is just the service — the address is the product. A new **Configure a model** section then names the two screens involved, because "set a task model" alone does not tell anyone where the API key goes: **Model registry** for the provider, Base URL and API key, then **Global defaults** to select that model as the task model.

## Real download links

`Install` now links release 0.2.0 directly, with a copy-pasteable `curl` for x86_64 and the aarch64 asset beside it. Both asset URLs and the release page were checked and return 200.

## The CLI, introduced

Both READMEs gain a short `Command line` section, and `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` gains the `run` subcommand section ported from the Chinese guide — the `run` line in the command list, the two-terminal example, the text/jsonl mode split, and the `--auto-approve` requirement for non-interactive runs. Those two rules are the ones a first scripted attempt fails on, so they are stated rather than left to `--help`.

## One deliberate omission, for a maintainer to decide

The "over 300 cross-domain Skills" figure is **not** carried over. It appeared only in the two READMEs — no source anywhere in the repository or the docs, while `skills/` ships 18. The capability is still described ("a cross-domain skill library"); only the unsourced number is gone. If the figure is one we stand behind, please restore it with a reference rather than taking my restatement as the final word — it is a marketing claim, not mine to adjudicate.

## Validation

Layers were run on `b87ca7bb` in a clean detached worktree of that commit. The pushed head `ead7cc6a` differs from it only in the two READMEs — the hero image reference, a Configure a model section, and the browser address after `serve` in the two READMEs — two markdown lines, no code — so the layer results carry over; the documentation checks below were re-run on `ead7cc6a`. Host is macOS (Darwin), which has no bubblewrap, so the two sandbox-dependent layers could not run here — stated below rather than substituted.

| Layer | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm ci:ut` | **Not runnable on this host.** Its guest tier executes a real bubblewrap sandbox, which does not exist on macOS. Ran `ci:ut:host` instead — not a substitute, reported as such. |
| `pnpm ci:ut:host` | **Failed at `pnpm ci:selftest`, on a pre-existing failure** (attribution below). Everything before it green: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `uv sync` for gateway and paper, `pnpm build`, `pnpm architecture:check` (8/8 tests, 275 package source files, "Architecture boundaries OK"), `pnpm typecheck`. Because the layer aborts at `ci:selftest`, the package tests and Python suites did not run on this host. |
| `pnpm ci:st` | **Passed**, exit 0, 25.7s. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm build`, `bash test/api/run_m1_smoke.sh` → `Agent loop smoke PASS: first-step tools + native loop + streaming model transport + real tool round-trip + multi-turn history verified.` |
| `pnpm ci:e2e` | **Not runnable on this host** — same bubblewrap requirement. |

### The `ci:selftest` failure is pre-existing

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

基于 `origin/main`（`425e4219`，已含 #137）从零实测 Docker Compose 部署：仓库自带 `Dockerfile` 冷构建、起栈、健康检查、浏览器登录、沙箱探针、同机多实例都能跑通，但新用户按现有文档会在几处卡住，文档也没有完整列出可配置的环境变量和常见问题。本 PR 把 Docker 部署指南重写成从构建到浏览器登录的完整步骤，补齐变量表与 FAQ，修一处 Compose 转发缺口，并把 Docker 分发路径纳入 GitHub Actions 守护。

1. **部署指南（中英同步）**：Docker 节改为「前置条件 → 准备配置与数据目录 → 构建 → 启动并确认健康 → 浏览器连接 → 配置模型」五步，之后是日常管理表、数据目录、多实例、环境变量、沙箱要求、常见问题（16 条）与限制。实测发现并写进文档的四个坑：bind mount 目录不先 `mkdir -p` 时 Docker 以 root 建目录，入口以「目录不可写」退出——多实例命令原来缺这一步，照抄必失败；日志里的登录链接端口固定是容器端口 4310，改了 `SCIENCE_AGENT_PUBLISH_PORT` 后要替换；首次启动会在后台创建 starter Python 环境（约 2 GB、需访问 conda-forge），不是卡住；镜像不含 evolve 与 memory-graph 边车，这两项功能在 Docker 中不可用。
2. **环境变量分层**：编排层只被 Compose 读取（`COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_IMAGE`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_DATA_HOST_DIR`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_UID` / `GID`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_PUBLISH_HOST` / `PORT`），容器层经 `environment` 块逐个转发，镜像层由 `Dockerfile` 固定。配置参考的 Docker 表按此拆分并补齐；未转发的变量（如 `HTTP_PROXY`）说明用 `docker-compose.override.yml` 追加。
3. **Compose 转发缺口**：配置参考把 `SCIENCE_AGENT_USAGE_EXCHANGE_RATE*` 四个键和 `SCIENCE_AGENT_MICROMAMBA_BASE_URL` 列为 Docker 变量，但 `docker-compose.yml` 都没有转发，设了静默无效（与 #137 修的上下文变量同类）。四个汇率键改为转发并加入 `.env.docker.example`，空值等于内置默认（`config.ts` 的解析函数对空串返回默认值）；micromamba 镜像 URL 从 Docker 表删除——镜像已内置并播种固定版本，运行期不下载。

### 🚀 Background Description


The coverage job currently generates and uploads Node.js and Python JSON summary artifacts, but the Actions run page does not expose the results directly. Contributors must download artifacts to see what was scanned and the aggregate coverage, unlike E2E results that are visible in the run summary.

This feature should make coverage results visible without introducing a minimum percentage gate.

### Design Ideas

Write a repository-owned Markdown renderer to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` from the existing `coverage/summary.json` and `coverage/python/summary.json`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Show Node.js and Python separately.
- Label full, incremental, skipped, failed, or unavailable scans.
- Show measured files/groups and available line, branch, and function totals.
- List selected groups for incremental scans.
- Keep coverage informational: no minimum percentage.
- Preserve current failure semantics and artifact uploads.

### Involved Public APIs

None. This changes only GitHub Actions reporting and repository-owned CI scripts.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

The change touches `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the existing Node.js/Python coverage scripts and selector rules, and the operational CI contract in `.ci/README.md`. Runtime APIs and product behavior are unaffected.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Unit-test the summary renderer for full, incremental, skipped, failed, and unavailable results.
- Test that changes to the renderer select full Node.js and Python coverage.
- Parse the workflow YAML after editing.
- Run the WSL build, recursive workspace tests, and architecture checks.
- Confirm coverage remains informational and coverage test failures still fail the job.

### Additional Information

An implementation is prepared on `wyhohyw:codex/coverage-actions-summary`; a Draft PR will link this issue.

### 🚀 Background Description


ScienceDiscovery contains maintained Python services whose tests are not represented by the Node.js coverage percentage. A Node-only number must not be presented as whole-repository coverage.

This issue adds a separate Python coverage pipeline using mature Python tooling. It complements the Node.js coverage issue #137 while keeping the two languages' commands, reports, and scope independently auditable.

### Design Ideas

### Measurement

- Use `coverage.py` as the coverage engine; do not implement a custom Python tracer.
- Preserve existing test frameworks:
  - `services/gateway` and `services/paper`: `unittest`
  - `services/memory-graph` and `services/evolve`: `pytest`
- Run each existing suite under `coverage run --branch --parallel-mode`, then use `coverage combine`.
- Measure production source directories, not test files.
- Record covered/total counts and percentages for lines and branches. Keep service/path groups separate.

### CI execution

- Reuse existing CI and nightly workflows rather than adding a standalone coverage workflow.
- PR/default-branch runs should select affected Python services where the dependency/selector mapping is reliable. A partial run must be explicitly marked partial and must never be displayed as whole-Python coverage.
- The existing nightly run should execute the complete Python coverage scope and publish the authoritative baseline.
- Coverage remains informational initially; existing test failures still fail the job.

### Reports and artifact

- Generate `coverage.py` JSON as the structured source consumed by the board.
- Optionally generate Cobertura XML for future GitHub Code Quality integration and LCOV/HTML for local diagnosis, without making a paid GitHub feature a prerequisite.
- Upload one SHA-qualified Actions artifact containing aggregate and per-service JSON summaries plus run identity metadata.
- Use repository default artifact retention.

### Dashboard

- Display Node.js and Python coverage as separate first-class metrics.
- If an overall line percentage is shown, compute it from summed covered/total lines:
  `(node covered + python covered) / (node total + python total)`.
- Never average percentages directly.
- Label nightly baselines as authoritative and partial/incremental results explicitly.

### Involved Public APIs

No product runtime or public API changes are proposed.

This feature adds an internal Python coverage artifact contract. It should align with the Node summary's run/SHA/mode/group metadata while retaining Python-specific metrics and source paths.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `services/gateway` and `services/paper` keep their existing `unittest` commands.
- `services/memory-graph` and `services/evolve` keep their existing `pytest` commands and extras.
- CI test selection and nightly scheduling determine whether the result is partial or authoritative.
- The status board consumes the structured Actions artifact; it does not run Python tests itself.
- GitHub Code Quality can consume Cobertura XML later, but this feature must work without enabling the paid service.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Add focused coverage runs for every maintained Python service and verify existing tests still execute with the same pass/fail semantics.
- Test combining parallel coverage data from `unittest` and `pytest` environments.
- Verify branch coverage is enabled and test files are excluded from production totals.
- Verify missing/failed service runs cannot produce an authoritative aggregate.
- Verify partial PR results and complete nightly baselines have distinct metadata.
- Validate JSON totals against `coverage report` for representative services.
- Add board parser/rendering tests for Python-only, Node-only, combined, missing, and stale artifacts.
- Verify overall coverage uses summed covered/total values, not the arithmetic mean of percentages.
- Run the complete repository test suite before merging.

### Additional Information

Related work:

- Node.js coverage tracking: #137
- Node.js WIP implementation: #134
- Companion status-board PR: https://github.com/ScienceDiscovery/github-status-board/pull/1
- coverage.py documentation: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/

Non-goals: migrating all Python tests to one framework, implementing a custom coverage engine, or requiring GitHub Code Quality/another paid service.

### 🚀 Background Description


ScienceDiscovery runs Node.js tests in CI but does not yet publish a durable, machine-readable coverage result tied to the exact workflow run and commit. Maintainers should be able to inspect coverage in GitHub Actions, while the status board should consume the same CI evidence without running tests itself or parsing unstable console text.

This issue covers **Node.js coverage only**. Python coverage should be tracked separately so that the tools, test commands, scope, and percentages remain explicit.

The current work-in-progress implementation is PR #134.

### Design Ideas

### Measurement

- Reuse the repository's existing built Node.js tests; do not introduce another test tier or migrate test frameworks.
- Run them with Node.js 22's built-in `--experimental-test-coverage` collector (V8 coverage).
- Group results by workspace/path and keep repository CI-script tests as explicit groups.
- Exclude test sources from production-source totals.
- Record covered/total counts and percentages for lines, branches, and functions rather than storing percentages alone.

### CI execution

- Integrate coverage into the existing `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; do not add a second coverage workflow.
- For pull requests and default-branch pushes, select changed Node.js workspaces and their transitive dependents. Changes to shared coverage infrastructure select every group.
- Reuse the existing nightly workflow for a complete, authoritative all-group baseline.
- Skip coverage for release-only calls.
- Test failures still fail the job. Coverage percentages are informational initially and do not introduce a new threshold gate.

### Actions artifact

- Generate LCOV only as a local intermediate.
- Upload one SHA-qualified artifact containing aggregate and per-group JSON summaries.
- Include source SHA, base SHA, generation time, mode (`incremental` or `full`), selected groups, and whether the result is authoritative.
- Use the repository's default artifact retention; do not introduce independent 30/90-day policies.

### Status-board consumption

- The board downloads the structured summary through the GitHub Actions Artifacts API. It does not execute tests and does not infer coverage from log text.
- Show the latest full nightly baseline, per-path line/branch/function coverage, nightly history, and recent PR affected-group results.
- A homepage value composed from later default-branch group summaries must be labelled as an estimate until the next full nightly run recalibrates it.

### Involved Public APIs

No product runtime or public API changes are proposed.

The feature adds an internal CI artifact contract for coverage summaries. Consumers must treat the run identity, SHA, mode, selected groups, and authoritative flag as part of that contract.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Existing CI and nightly workflows provide the execution environment.
- Existing Node workspace dependency metadata is used to expand changed workspaces to transitive dependents.
- The companion status board reads the Actions artifact and renders the coverage page.
- Browser/TSX, Python, and Playwright coverage are explicitly excluded from this issue and must not be represented as covered by the Node percentage.
- GitHub Code Quality/Cobertura upload can be evaluated separately; it is not required for the initial board integration.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Add selector tests for changed workspaces, transitive dependents, shared-infrastructure full selection, and irrelevant-path skips.
- Add aggregation tests that exclude test sources and preserve aggregate and per-group covered/total values.
- Validate that PR/default-branch CI publishes affected-group summaries from the existing CI workflow.
- Validate that nightly publishes a complete authoritative baseline without a second workflow.
- Verify that every artifact is tied to its workflow run/SHA and contains only the structured JSON required by consumers.
- Verify that test failures still fail the coverage job.
- Add status-board tests distinguishing authoritative nightly data, incremental/PR data, estimates, and UT/ST/E2E artifacts.
- Run the repository's complete existing test suite before merging.

### Additional Information

Related work:

- WIP implementation: #134
- Companion status-board PR: https://github.com/ScienceDiscovery/github-status-board/pull/1
- Design in the implementation branch: `docs/designs/test-coverage.v3.md`

Acceptance boundary: the resulting percentage covers built Node.js workspace tests and repository CI-script tests only. It must never be presented as whole-repository coverage.

  by linking the tutorial, and the tutorial's Next section links back), so the overlap
  there is already settled.
- `docs/architecture/` (3 files) overlaps in topic with the explanation architecture pages
  and is linked from shipped documentation (`deployment.md:350`, `configuration.md:107`,
  `agent-backend.md:273`), but it is not listed in the documentation indexes and is excluded
  from the site's all-documents view, so its publication status is unclear.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:440` still describes `docs/` as Chinese-only, which is out of date for
  the bilingual tree.

## What to write

1. Fix the blank-line and index-list defects in the four files above.
2. Decide the canonical status of `docs/architecture/` (internal design record or published
   explanation) and label or link it accordingly in the indexes.
3. Update the stale `CONTRIBUTING.md` sentence to describe the bilingual tree.
4. Run a minimum Markdown check over `docs/` (fenced code blocks closed, heading levels not
   skipping, relative links resolving, images carrying alt text) and record the chosen
   checker and command in the change that fixes the defects.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The formatting defects in the four files above are fixed.
- [ ] `docs/architecture/` has a recorded status, and the indexes match that decision.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` describes the documentation tree correctly.
- [ ] The chosen Markdown check is recorded and passes over `docs/`.

## Open questions

- Is `docs/architecture/` maintained as an internal record (keep, label, exclude from
  indexes) or should it merge into `explanation/`? This needs a content owner.
- Which Markdown checker should be the recorded default?

## Out of scope

- Rewriting stable explanation pages to shorten them.
- Terminology and UI-label alignment across languages (owned by the bilingual-gaps issue).
- Any evolve content work (owned by #55).

- [ ] L2 event golden trace: scripted scenarios (tool call, approval, interrupt, sub-agent, error, reconnect and resume) record the old backend's SSE
- [ ] Re-check the Gateway protocol against JiuwenSwarm 0.2.6: `chat.send` parameter keys, payload keys of each response and event, behavior when multiple clients subscribe to the same session, behavior after a disconnect
- [ ] Fault injection: verify whether JiuwenSwarm's error channels (`ok:false` in `res`, `chat.error`, `execution.error`, `runtime.error`) reach the frontend in full
- [ ] Calibrate the 59 "approximate mappings" and the event mapping in #84, and write the conclusions back to each sub-task
- [ ] Evaluate the `AgentRuntime` componentization interface as input for the long-term cutover

### To be confirmed

- The list of 10 E2E cases (Zhang Yi, Sep 21)
- How the stub LLM connects to JiuwenSwarm's model configuration

- [ ] The events involved have L2 golden traces
- [ ] The corresponding E2E cases, to be added once the list of 10 cases is set

## Summary

ScienceMemory currently only works if the user installs and runs an external **Neo4j 5.x** server. That is a heavy prerequisite for what is, in most local runs, a small per-session graph. I would like a **fallback backend that persists the graph as plain text files on the local disk** and is used automatically when Neo4j is not configured or not reachable, with Neo4j kept as the opt-in backend for larger/shared deployments.

## Current behaviour

Per `docs/en/how-to/science-memory-setup.md`:

- None of the three deployment modes (single-file binary, Docker, source local mode) bundle Neo4j — ScienceMemory "needs an external Neo4j server".
- The user has to either run `docker run ... neo4j:5` or add the Neo4j apt/dnf repo and `systemctl enable --now neo4j`, then set an initial password and fill in HTTP address / user / password in System configuration → Memory.
- Until that is done, the feature stays off: health reports `needs-password`, or `degraded` when Neo4j is unreachable, and nothing is recorded.

In code the coupling is total: everything under `services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/` speaks Cypher over Neo4j's HTTP Transactional API — roughly 160 `MERGE`/`MATCH` statements in `persistence.py`, 45 in `query.py`, 39 in `search_graph.py`, plus `constraints.py`, all going through the single `Neo4jHandle` in `neo4j_driver.py`.

## Why this is a problem

1. **Install cost is out of proportion to the data.** A typical session's graph is a few hundred Task / ToolCall / Code / Artifact / Paper / WebPage nodes and their edges. Standing up a JVM graph database (plus a container runtime or a distro package + systemd unit + initial password) to hold that is a lot of setup for a single-user local run.
2. **Many target environments cannot do it.** Offline / air-gapped clusters, shared login nodes without root or Docker, corporate laptops with restricted package sources, CI sandboxes — in all of these the documented install paths (Docker Hub pull, `deb.neo4j.com` / `dnf` repo, `sudo systemctl`) are simply unavailable.
3. **Silent degradation makes it look broken.** The graceful degrade is the right default, but the net effect for a new user is that a documented feature quietly records nothing, and the only way out is a multi-step external install.
4. **It blocks the "just try it" path.** Someone evaluating ScienceDiscovery from the binary or `start-stack.sh` cannot see provenance/traceability — the thing ScienceMemory exists to demonstrate — without first becoming a Neo4j operator.

## Proposal

Introduce a storage-backend seam and ship a Neo4j-free default.

1. **Backend interface.** `neo4j_driver.handle` / `session()` is already the single chokepoint that `persistence` / `query` / `constraints` / `search_graph` / `server` go through (the HTTP session deliberately mirrors the Bolt `Session`/`Result`/`Record` surface). Turn that into an explicit backend protocol rather than a Neo4j-specific handle.
2. **Local file backend (new default).** Persist nodes and edges as human-readable text under the existing data directory — e.g. append-only JSONL (`nodes.jsonl`, `edges.jsonl`) per session or per workspace, or a single JSON graph document. This is a good fit because:
   - all writes are already `MERGE` on a unique key and idempotent across retries, so an append log with last-write-wins on the key replays cleanly;
   - the read side is a bounded, known set of queries (session chain, artifact lineage, citation/evidence chain, search), not arbitrary Cypher — they can be served by an in-memory index built from the file on load;
   - the data volume is small enough to hold in memory for the lifetime of the sidecar.
   (If a pure-text file turns out to be too weak for the query side, an embedded SQLite/`kuzu` store would still remove the external-server requirement — but a text format has the extra benefit of being greppable, diffable, and easy to attach to a bug report or commit.)
3. **Selection rules.** Backend chosen by configuration: `local` (default, no credentials needed) vs `neo4j` (current behaviour). When Neo4j is configured but unreachable, either keep degrading as today or fall back to the local backend — whichever the maintainers prefer — but the *unconfigured* case should land on `local` and report `healthy`, not `needs-password`.
4. **Migration / export.** A one-way importer from the local file store into Neo4j, so a user who starts locally and later outgrows it can move their history over.

## Benefits

- ScienceMemory works out of the box in all three deployment modes, with zero external services.
- Works in offline, rootless, and container-less environments.
- The graph becomes inspectable with ordinary tools (`grep`, `jq`, a diff) and easy to share when reporting a problem.
- Neo4j remains available and unchanged for users who want its scale and its browser/query tooling.

## Open questions

- Preferred on-disk format: JSONL append log, single JSON document, or something else already used elsewhere in the repo?
- Scope of the local backend: per-session files, or one store for all sessions with a session index?
- Should the local backend serve the same `/health` states, adding something like `healthy (local)`, or reuse `healthy` as-is?

Happy to prototype the backend seam plus a JSONL implementation if the direction is acceptable.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Provide a Neo4j-free fallback for ScienceMemory — persist the graph as local text files

## Summary

The web UI has a solid i18n system — 2442 English keys and 2441 Chinese ones, with only a `test.englishFallback` key missing — but three places sit outside it. The visible result: **an English-locale user gets a half-Chinese Idea Tree**.

## 1. Idea Tree renders hardcoded Chinese regardless of locale

`detectLocale()` in `apps/web/src/i18n/locale.ts` returns `en` for any browser whose `navigator.languages` does not start with `zh`, so this is the default path for non-Chinese users, not an edge case. These strings are Chinese literals in JSX, never passed through `t()`:

| File | Hardcoded lines | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| `IdeaResearchCard.tsx` | 14 | `重试`, `重新连接`, `暂停`, `继续`, `查看研究进度 →`, `第 {r.round} / {maxRounds} 轮` |
| `IdeaResearchLabels.ts` | 11 | `构思方向与改进`, `设计候选`, `聚合评估`, `已中断`, `正在暂停` |
| `IdeaTreeSettingsEditor.tsx` | 9 | `科研模板`, `通用科研假设探索`, `水处理材料设计`, `快速：少量路径，快速判断` |
| `IdeaTreeExplorer.tsx` | 5 | — |
| `IdeaResearchTimelineCard.tsx` | 5 | `Idea Tree 研究已启动`, `正在读取实时进度…`, `节点 {id}` |
| `IdeaTreeView.tsx` | 1 | `查看旧树（只读） →` |
| `IdeaTreeCanvas.tsx` | 1 | `方向` |

What makes this jarring rather than merely untranslated: **the other half of the same feature is translated.** `ideaTree.phase.preflight_research`, `ideaTree.phase.building_tree`, `ideaTree.maxDepth`, `ideaTree.maxRounds` and friends all live in the catalog. So an English user sees "Building Idea Tree" and "Max depth" next to `暂停`, `继续`, and `第 1 / 5 轮` in the same panel.

Some of these are also inline object literals rather than keys, e.g. in both `IdeaResearchCard.tsx` and `IdeaResearchTimelineCard.tsx`:

```
{running: "执行中", completed: "已完成", stopped: "已停止", failed: "失败"}[activity.status]
```

## 2. `plugins/settings.tsx` implements its own translation mechanism

Eight sites use inline ternaries instead of the catalog:

```
<summary>{zh ? "可选扩展" : "Optional extensions"}</summary>
<option value="enabled">{zh ? "启用" : "Enabled"}</option>
```

and the plugin manifest table carries parallel `name`/`zh` and `description`/`descriptionZh` fields. It works today, but it is a second translation system running beside a 2442-key catalog: new strings land in whichever one the author happens to touch, and nothing keeps the two in sync.

## 3. A reviewable subset of the catalog is untranslated

49 keys have byte-identical English and Chinese values. Many are correct — `Gemini`, `DeepSeek`, `MiniMax`, `OpenAI Chat Completions`, `Anthropic Messages`, `Client ID`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `English`, `{celsius} °C`. But these look like genuine gaps:

- **Memory graph relation labels**, the entire set: `node.relation.produces` = "produces", `.next` = "next", `.extracts` = "extracts", `.supports` = "supports", `.stated_in` = "stated in", `.supersedes` = "supersedes", `.input` = "input". Every edge label in the Chinese memory-graph view is English.
- **Idea Tree prompt labels**: `ideaTree.designPrompt` = "Designer prompt", `.assessorPrompt` = "Assessor system prompt", `.aggregatorPrompt` = "Aggregator prompt".
- **Common nouns**: `settings.skills` / `search.skills` / `settings.groups.skills.label` / `skillManager.tabSkills` = "Skills"; `runtime.status.runner` / `runnerWorkspaces.runnerLabel` = "Runner"; `remote.runnersTitle` = "Runners"; `subagent.role` = "SubAgent"; `skillManager.eyebrow` = "Agent Skills".
- **Interpolated labels**: `app.epoch` = "Epoch {id}", `skillLibrary.head` = "Head {id}", `settings.skillLibraryHead` = "Head {version}", `runnerWorkspaces.agentId` = "Agent {id}", `subagent.tokens` = "{count} tokens", `csv.schemaVersion` = "schema v{version}", `evolve.chart.rollout` = "rollout".

## Reproduction

1. Open the UI in a browser whose language is not Chinese (or set the language switch to English).
2. Start an Idea Tree research run.
3. The research card, timeline card, and Idea Tree settings render Chinese labels and buttons.

## Suggested fix

1. Move every user-visible Idea Tree string into `messages.ts` and call `t()`, including the inline status maps in `IdeaResearchCard.tsx` and `IdeaResearchTimelineCard.tsx` and the label maps in `IdeaResearchLabels.ts`.
2. Fold `plugins/settings.tsx` into the catalog, and decide whether plugin manifests should carry per-locale display names or catalog keys.
3. Translate the subset in §3 — the `node.relation.*` set in particular, since it is every edge label in the memory graph.
4. **Add a guard.** The repository already runs static checks via `pnpm architecture:check` (`scripts/check-architecture.mjs`, `scripts/component-boundaries.mjs`). A check in the same spirit — fail on a CJK string literal in `apps/web/src/**/*.tsx` outside `i18n/` and outside comments — would keep this from coming back. Today that check would flag 45 lines across 7 files, all listed above.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Idea Tree feature renders fully in English under the `en` locale and fully in Chinese under `zh-CN`.
- [ ] No user-visible string bypasses the message catalog (plugin settings included).
- [ ] The `node.relation.*` labels are translated.
- [ ] A static check fails the build when a new hardcoded CJK literal appears in a component.

### 🚀 背景描述

Ascend 910B 上，主机 `npu-smi` 可以把每张卡都报成 Health OK，但同一张卡放进 bubblewrap 沙箱后经常打不开。原因是：进程进入 mount namespace 之后，昇腾驱动按调用者 `/dev` 里看得见的卡做枚举，而且是全有或全无——任意一张当时占不上的卡，会让整次 `drvGetDevNum` 失败（例如 `DRV_ERROR_RESOURCE_OCCUPIED`）。把宿主整个 `/dev` 绑进沙箱，在共享机器上几乎必然失败。

产品需要的结果是：操作员能从 Runner 状态看到卡的状态和占用，只勾选**能在沙箱里打开**的卡，勾选的卡绑进沙箱后编号从 0 开始，沙箱内能跑 `npu-smi info` 以及 MindSpore / torch-npu。本次只适配 910B。实现见合并请求 [#107](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/pull/107)。

### 设计思路

考虑过、并放弃的路：

- 把宿主 `/dev` 整棵绑进沙箱：驱动会一次看到所有卡，共享机上必挂。
- 用 `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` 做逻辑重映射：它作用在 CANN 运行时之上，挡不住驱动层枚举失败。
- 把作业改到宿主 NPU Broker（不进沙箱）：现有 Broker 继续服务白名单 workload，但不能冒充「沙箱内可用」。

选定做法：

1. **逐卡探针**。对每张卡起一个一次性沙箱，只 bind 这一张卡，在里面跑 `npu-smi info`。退出码 0 才标 `sandboxUsable`；失败时带上驱动原文。探针与正式 launch 使用同一套 namespace、`--cap-drop ALL`、全新 `--dev /dev`。
2. **勾选面**。Remote compute 里每个 Runner（含本机 `local`）列出全部卡：可用可勾，不可用禁用并给出原因。选择按 Runner id 持久化。保存时向该 Runner **现场要清单**，不读从未落盘的连接态。
3. **执行接线**。每次 Python / shell / 托管 shell 按目标 Runner 把已勾选卡号放进请求；Runner 启动前再校验。空勾选则请求里没有该字段，沙箱与无 NPU 时一致。
4. **绑定与编号**。保持 `--dev /dev`，对选中卡做 `--dev-bind /dev/davinci<host> /dev/davinci<sandbox>`，按 host 下标升序映射到 0..n-1。管理节点（`davinci_manager`、`devmm_svm`、`hisi_hdc`）按主机实际存在的绑定。有 NPU 时 PATH 才加上 `/usr/local/bin`，以便调用 `npu-smi`；无 NPU 时 PATH 不变。
5. **隔离不放宽**。仍是 `--unshare-all --unshare-user --cap-drop ALL` 与既有 seccomp。

共享机上「勾选时可用、稍后被占」是预期场景：启动时若卡已不可用，执行按卡号失败，而不是掉进框架深处。

### 涉及到的对外API

产品 HTTP（非公开 SDK 承诺，但是操作面用到的接口）：

- `GET /api/runners/npu`：本机清单 + 各 Runner 勾选。
- `PUT /api/runners/:runnerId/npu-devices`：保存勾选；含不可用卡时 409，并带驱动原因。
- 发给 Runner 的 Python / shell 执行请求增加可选字段 `npuDevices`（宿主卡号数组）。
- Runner `GET /resources`、`GET /npu/devices` 携带 NPU 清单。

未改 Host NPU Broker 的作业接口。

### 与其他模块的相关性描述

- 沙箱启动（bubblewrap argv、seccomp、能力丢弃）必须保持 fail-closed。
- Remote compute / 本机 Runner 卡片共用勾选控件。
- Provenance 把 `npuDevices` 原样 POST 给 Runner，不能在中间层丢掉。
- 执行签名窗口仍默认 30s；时钟差只能用 `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTION_SIGNATURE_MAX_AGE_MS` 显式加宽。

### 测试设计与测试计划

- 单测：探针 argv、进程表误解析、勾选规则、从 0 重编号、无勾选时沙箱 `/dev` 无 davinci、有勾选时 bind 来自请求、四条执行路径带上 `npuDevices`、HMAC 默认 30s、PUT 现场问 Runner。
- 浏览器旅程 J7（mocked）：列出卡、不可用禁用、按 Runner 保存、重开保持、390px 无横向溢出。
- 910B 真机：勾选可用卡后产品 `run_shell` 在沙箱内 `npu-smi info` 成功；清空勾选后无 davinci、`npu-smi` 不在 PATH。
- 回归：既有 Host Broker 路径零改动。

### 其他信息

对应实现：[feat: 将 910B NPU 卡交给沙箱使用](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/pull/107)。

items.body:
## Summary and current-release boundary

Multi-agent orchestration is a core JiuwenSwarm capability. ScienceDiscovery should explicitly evaluate whether and how to reuse it, rather than silently treating our existing orchestration as the final architecture.

For this release, retain the currently validated hybrid path: **ScienceDiscovery manages delegation through `task`; JiuwenSwarm executes both the main agent and the child agents.** This RFC does not request an immediate migration or block the current release. The eventual reuse decision must be documented with implementation evidence, validation results, and trade-offs.

## Current implementation

The current debugging deployment explicitly selects the platform `task` route. This is a deployment choice, not a claim that every Swarm-backed deployment uses this route.

```text
Main agent (Swarm loop)
  -> ScienceDiscovery task orchestration
  -> Child agent (independent Swarm loop)
  -> Platform task result
  -> Main agent continues
```

ScienceDiscovery currently prepares the specialist profile, enabled MCP/skills, workspace and handoff; manages permissions, concurrency, turn/time limits and cancellation; and records child progress, results and artifacts for the existing UI. The parent receives the result when the `task` call completes.

Swarm's native route uses `subagent_spawn` and `subagent_wait`, with Swarm owning child orchestration. Its integration with ScienceDiscovery-specific bindings has not been fully validated. This does **not** mean Swarm lacks tools, permissions or lifecycle management; the question is how its mechanisms map to the platform's existing behavior.

## Problem and existing evidence

Using Swarm only as the execution engine leaves an important part of its core capability unreused, while switching delegation tools alone risks losing platform behavior. We need a deliberate ownership boundary instead of two overlapping orchestration systems.

A recent real-LLM literature-research run completed through platform `task`: two Swarm-executed children used professional literature MCP tools, returned results, and the parent produced a registered report. This validates that hybrid route only; it does not establish native `subagent_spawn` MCP inheritance, comparative quality, or benchmark-wide reliability.

## Evaluation scope

Evaluate the native route against the current hybrid baseline on the same pinned versions and comparable model/task/tool settings.

| Area | Questions to resolve |
| --- | --- |
| Delegation and scheduling | Who owns creation, concurrency, waiting, completion, and nested delegation? Can we avoid duplicate schedulers and inconsistent state? |
| Context and capabilities | How do specialist instructions, skills, model selection and enabled MCP tools reach each child's actual LLM input? What is inherited versus explicitly handed off? |
| Workspace and science outputs | How do child workspace isolation, sandbox paths, artifact registration, provenance and parent access map to Swarm? |
| Permissions and lifecycle | How are manual approval, automatic approval, cancellation, turn/time limits and partial failures preserved? |
| Results and UI | How are streaming child progress, tool events, usage, errors and final results represented in the existing UI? Does the parent reliably continue? |
| Maintenance | Which extension points already exist? Which minimal upstream fixes/hooks are missing? What platform code could actually be removed? |

Prefer native Swarm capabilities for generic agent behavior. Keep differentiated science functionality in separate modules; intrusive Swarm changes should be limited to bug fixes or necessary extension hooks, not embedding science business logic.

## Candidate outcomes — not a predetermined selection

1. **Native Swarm orchestration plus science extensions:** reuse spawning/waiting/lifecycle and adapt platform capabilities and UI events.
2. **Staged migration:** retain `task` temporarily while closing named native-integration gaps, then transfer ownership with clear exit criteria.
3. **Retain platform orchestration:** acceptable only with concrete evidence explaining why native reuse is unsuitable, its maintenance costs, and conditions for revisiting the decision.

A tool rename or a single successful demo is insufficient to choose between these options.

## Validation and required conclusion

The decision should be backed by deterministic integration tests and a small set of comparable real research runs, not only code inspection.

- Verify actual child LLM tool lists, model routing, skill/context delivery and workspace access.
- Cover parallel children, successful result collection and parent continuation, one child failing, timeout/cancellation, and both approval modes.
- Verify child artifacts remain accessible and traceable, and UI progress reaches a correct terminal state.
- Compare task completion, result quality, token use, elapsed time and resource consumption under comparable conditions; record limitations and failures.

Before closing this RFC, publish a community-reviewed conclusion containing:

- the selected architecture and the rationale for reusing or not reusing native Swarm orchestration;
- a capability/gap matrix with concrete source or test evidence;
- ownership of scheduling, context/tool binding, permissions, lifecycle and science outputs;
- required changes, migration and rollback boundaries, and code that can be removed;
- remaining limitations and follow-up issues, with an explicit distinction between current-release acceptance and the long-term decision.

Related: #84 (Swarm migration), #107 (E2E scenarios).
items.title: [RFC] Evaluate native JiuwenSwarm multi-agent orchestration versus the current platform task integration

### 📚 Documentation Issue Description

> Related: #116 (first-run installation troubleshooting), #118 (capability entries), #119 (entry-point order). The landing pages and the bucket definitions overlap with #119's navigation ask, so this issue owns their delivery and #119 owns the ordering.

## Summary

PR 122 reorganizes the docs into six buckets per language, but the scaffolding that makes a bucket usable is missing. Five of the six buckets have no landing page, the meaning of each bucket is written only in the PR description, and the user tree has no security page, no general FAQ and no glossary. I would like these standard pages added on top of the structure PR 122 ships.

## Current state

Verified against 0e904661:

- Twelve content directories (six buckets, two languages), and only `developer-docs` has a README in each language. `getting-started`, `core`, `domains`, `how-to` and `reference` have none, so a reader who jumps to a bucket lands on a bare file list.
- What each bucket is for exists only in the PR 122 description. `docs/README.md` names the six buckets in one sentence and defines none of them. Names like `core` and `domains` are not self-explanatory.
- No security or trust page exists in the user tree. The only security text is the multi-user WARNING in `README.md:85-86` (and `README_zh.md:85-86`), which covers loopback binding, the single bearer token, the absence of TLS and the sandbox boundary. The one page that explains isolation, `sandbox-execution.md`, sits in `docs/en/developer-docs/` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/`.
- No general troubleshooting or FAQ page exists. Troubleshooting exists only as per-task sections: the Docker section inside `docs/en/getting-started/deployment.md`, short `## Troubleshooting` sections in `docs/en/how-to/configure-custom-mcp.md:91` and `docs/en/how-to/run-with-jiuwenswarm.md:103`, and a `## 5. Troubleshooting` section in `docs/en/how-to/science-memory-setup.md:187`. The first-run, installation-recovery path is already asked for in #116, which is narrower than a general FAQ.
- No glossary exists. Terms such as Project and Session (used in `docs/en/getting-started/quick-start.md:48`), and Skill, Specialist, Connector, Reviewer and workspace (used across `docs/en/reference/runtime-behavior.md`), have no single definition a new reader can look up.

## What to write

1. Section landing pages. Add a `README.md` to each of the five index-less buckets in both languages, using one template: what this bucket is for, when a reader should come here, and one line for each child page.
2. Bucket definitions. Write the six definitions into `docs/README.md`, so the classification rule lives in the repository and not only in the pull request.
3. Security and trust page. Add a user-facing page in both languages that states the loopback and single-token defaults, the absence of TLS, the fail-closed sandbox and what runs outside it, and the "not a multi-user service" boundary. Link `docs/en/developer-docs/sandbox-execution.md` for depth instead of repeating it.
4. General troubleshooting and FAQ. Add a page in both languages covering model connection failures, permission cards, connector and proxy failures, run timeouts, and where data lives. Keep first-run installation recovery in #116 and link to it.
5. Glossary. Add a page in both languages defining at least Project, Session, Skill, Specialist, Connector, Reviewer and workspace, and link it from the language index.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of `getting-started`, `core`, `domains`, `how-to` and `reference` has a landing page in both languages, following one template.
- [ ] `docs/README.md` defines what each of the six buckets is for.
- [ ] A security and trust page exists in both user trees and links the sandbox design page.
- [ ] A general troubleshooting or FAQ page exists in both languages and is distinct from the first-run recovery in #116.
- [ ] A glossary page defines at least Project, Session, Skill, Specialist, Connector, Reviewer and workspace.
- [ ] Each new page is linked from its language index, and each landing page links its child pages.

## Open questions

- Should the bucket definitions live in `docs/README.md`, in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, or on a dedicated documentation-style page?
- Does the security page need maintainer sign-off on what is safe to claim before it is published?
- Should the glossary be one page per language, or a section of the documentation home?

## Out of scope

- Page frontmatter and a page status or version schema.
- A machine-readable `llms.txt` or `llms-full.txt` export.
- Changelog or release-notes pages.

## Summary

Several capabilities have no user-facing entry point in the documentation, and PR #122
made the gap structural: it moved the capability pages into `developer-docs` and left
`core` nearly empty. A reader who finishes a first task cannot discover what else the
product does. I want short, verifiable entries for a first batch, plus one structural ask:
every confirmed capability should have at least one entry point on the user-facing side.

## Current state

Documentation-tree evidence at 0e904661:

- Idea Tree: the only page is `docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md` (34 lines, Chinese only). There
  is no `docs/en/core/idea-tree.md` and no how-to entry in either language.
  `docs/zh/README.md` lists the page under core, so Chinese readers have a route and
  English readers have none.
- Web providers: `docs/en/reference/web-tools.md` (69 lines) documents providers, but no
  how-to walks a reader from configuring a provider to a cited result.
- Skills and Specialists: the closest pages are
  `docs/en/developer-docs/skill-progressive-disclosure.md` and the long case in
  `docs/en/domains/literature-research.md`. There is no user-facing how-to for finding,
  enabling, trying, or scoping a skill, and specialists appear mainly in developer
  material.
- Usage: `docs/en/developer-docs/web-frontend.md:26` describes the usage dashboard with its
  filters and CSV/JSON export, but no user-facing page explains where the page is, what
  the numbers mean, or how to export.
- Structural evidence: PR #122's classification moved `science-memory.md`,
  `subagent-orchestration.md`, `skill-progressive-disclosure.md`, `science-connectors.md`,
  `review-provenance.md`, and `sandbox-execution.md` under `developer-docs`. `docs/en/core/`
  holds only `evolve.md` and `execution-workspaces.md` (the Chinese tree adds only
  `idea-tree.md`), yet the language index calls that section "Core capabilities". User
  coverage of the six capabilities named in the PR's own body is uneven. Connectors
  (section 3.1), skills (3.5) and the review/provenance views (section 7) already have
  user-facing routes in `domains/literature-research.md`, and ScienceMemory has
  `how-to/science-memory-setup.md`. Subagent orchestration and sandbox execution still
  have only developer-docs pages.

These are observations about the documentation tree, not claims of stable public support.
Confirmation is an open question below.

Implementation evidence, verified at 0e904661:

- Idea Tree settings and view components ship (`apps/web/src/App.tsx:229` imports
  `IdeaTreeSettingsEditor` and line 242 imports `IdeaTreeView`; the canvas component is

- A Web search and fetch settings group ships (`apps/web/src/App.tsx:777, 5057`).

  5090`).
- `UsagePage` ships (`apps/web/src/App.tsx:4327`) with filters and CSV/JSON export.

## What to write

1. Structural ask: give every confirmed capability at least one entry point in the
   user-facing buckets. The cheapest form is a capability map page in `core`, with one
   paragraph per capability linking to the deeper page in `developer-docs`. PR #122's body
   already acknowledges there is no concise core overview for ScienceMemory, subagents,
   skills, scientific connectors, or review/provenance.
2. Idea Tree: a user-facing entry plus an English page at `docs/en/core/idea-tree.md`,
   written from the Chinese source at `docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md`. This issue owns the
   English page.
3. Web providers: a how-to from configuring a provider to reading a cited search result.
4. Skills and Specialists: a how-to covering how to find, enable, try, and scope a skill,
   and when configuring a Specialist is worth it.
5. Usage: a how-to covering where the page is, what the columns mean, and how to export.

For the remaining candidates with unconfirmed status (Plugins, session trajectory, runner
inheritance, the skill-library design notes): record the product status (public /
experimental / internal) somewhere a maintainer can cite, and keep anything unconfirmed
out of the user path. Page-level disposition of the Chinese-only pages belongs to the
